title: Big Countries
statement:
One table describes countries:

- `World(name, continent, area, population, gdp)`: one row per country; `name` is unique. `area` is in square kilometres and `gdp` is the country's GDP.

Call a country **big** when its `area` is at least 3,000,000 or its `population` is at least 25,000,000 (either condition is enough, and both limits count as big). Report every big country once with the columns `name`, `population` and `area`, in that order. Rows may come in any order.
constraints: area, population and gdp are not negative
Both limits are inclusive: area >= 3000000 or population >= 25000000
reference:
SELECT w.name, w.population, w.area
FROM World AS w
WHERE w.area >= 3000000
   OR w.population >= 25000000;
brute:
SELECT name, population, area
FROM World
WHERE area >= 3000000
UNION
SELECT name, population, area
FROM World
WHERE population >= 25000000
notes:
## Intuition

Whether a country is big depends only on its own row, so no joins or grouping are needed: test each row against the two thresholds and keep it when **either** one is met. The work is all in writing the condition exactly: `OR` rather than `AND`, and `>=` rather than `>` because a country sitting exactly on a limit is big.

## Approach

1. Read every row of `World` (alias `w`).
2. Keep a row when `w.area >= 3000000` or `w.population >= 25000000`.
3. Select `name`, `population` and `area` in that order; `continent` and `gdp` play no part.

## Example 1, step by step

- Afghanistan: area 652,230 is small, but population 25,500,100 reaches the limit, so it is kept.
- Albania: 28,748 km² and 2,831,741 people, both below the limits, so it is dropped.
- Algeria: area 2,381,741 is below 3,000,000, but 37,100,000 people is enough, so it is kept.
- Andorra and Angola fail both tests (Angola has 1,246,700 km² and 20,609,294 people).

The result is Afghanistan and Algeria.

## Complexity

- Time: O(N) for N countries, one check per row (an index on each column could make the two parts faster as a `UNION`).
- Space: O(N) for the result in the worst case.

## Pitfalls

- `>` instead of `>=` drops countries exactly at 3,000,000 km² or 25,000,000 people.
- `AND` instead of `OR` keeps only countries that are big in both senses.
- Splitting the condition into two queries joined by `UNION ALL` reports a country that meets both conditions twice; plain `UNION` removes the duplicate.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `w` | `World`, one row per country |
| `w.area >= 3000000` | big by area |
| `w.population >= 25000000` | big by population |

narration.1: Report the name, population and area of each big country, in the required column order.
narration.2: Every country row is a candidate.
narration.3: A country covering at least 3,000,000 square kilometres is big.
narration.4: So is one with at least 25,000,000 people; OR means either condition is enough.
